name: Jether
overview: Jether is a male figure from the tribe of Manasseh, known primarily as the firstborn son of Gideon. His identity is succinctly noted in Scripture without additional personal details or narrative elaboration. There are no extra notes recorded about his life or character beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Jether appears as a proper name in Scripture but carries no specific meaning or divine origin indicated in the biblical text. It is simply the personal name given to Gideon's son.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jether as the son of Gideon, establishing his place within a significant family line. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Jether's significance lies chiefly in his role as the firstborn son of Gideon, a prominent judge and leader in Israel. While Jether himself is not the focus of any recorded deeds or teachings, his connection to Gideon situates him within the historical narrative of God's deliverance of Israel through chosen leaders. This familial link underscores the continuity of God's work through generations within the tribe of Manasseh.
